<reason>B won a close, high-quality clash by matching the motion to development rather than already-fielded kits, compounding CON’s “months” into a cycle-by-cycle gap, and turning CON’s industrial “emergency” plus the shared-fab pool into evidence the delay is real. A’s mature-node, prestige-foundry, and volume-learning attacks were sharp and better than B’s commercial-cost story, but they never fully showed that narrower tasks make the chokepoint militarily irrelevant.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Rebuttal 2: Q1 is a trick because fielded systems are already trained, then the emergency/budget-line contradiction plus “no separate military fab.” That pair did the most damage to A’s live route.</best_rebuttal>
